title: GuardDuty Finding Ingestion

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.8 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.8 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:guardduty` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:guardduty"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.8_guardduty_finding_ingest_8"
| sort -_time
description: GuardDuty provides ML-powered threat detection for AWS accounts. Centralizing findings in Splunk enables correlation with other security data.
value: Detecting guardduty finding ingestion early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable GuardDuty in all regions. Configure CloudWatch Events rule to forward findings to an SNS topic or S3. Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws. Alert on High/Critical findings (severity ≥7).
visualization: Table by severity, Bar chart (finding types), Trend line (findings over time), Single value.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Intrusion_Detection.IDS_Attacks
  where (match(lower(IDS_Attacks.severity), "high|critical|severe")
         OR (isnum(IDS_Attacks.severity) AND IDS_Attacks.severity >= 7))
  by IDS_Attacks.signature IDS_Attacks.severity IDS_Attacks.src span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Intrusion_Detection (IDS_Attacks) and Alerts: map `aws:cloudwatch:guardduty` fields into CIM when possible; else Step 2 on raw or HEC is primary. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Benign port scans, red-team, authorized network scanners, and new accounts/regions before suppressions and baselines are tuned.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:guardduty`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable GuardDuty in all regions. Configure CloudWatch Events rule to forward findings to an SNS topic or S3. Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws. Alert on High/Critical findings (severity ≥7).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:guardduty" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:guardduty"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.8_guardduty_finding_ingest_8"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:guardduty` in `index=aws` to detect guardduty finding ingestion. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_8_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table by severity, Bar chart (finding types), Trend line (findings over time), Single value..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of guardduty finding ingestion so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
